_about: Manifest for tools/audio/machine_clips.py. Sources are the operator's recordings (Desktop drop of 2026-09-22, moved to assets/audio/machines/_source/ on 2026-09-25 — gitignored, .gdignore'd). Every region/range below was MEASURED on the recording's RMS envelope (0.05–1 s hops) before being written down; the reasoning is in the note. Loops are RMS-normalised to rms_db so the .tres gain_db slider is the only place relative loudness lives.

clips.note: File name: take 17 s onwards — the region starts at exactly 17.0 s, as the name says (2026-09-25 review; it was 18.0). Envelope: -20 dB until 15.5 s, a step to -17 dB at 16 s (the sieve at full amplitude), steady to 57.5 s, then fades out (-25 .. -52 dB). 24 s loop cut from within 17-57 s.
File name: take 25-35 s exactly. That window is -26 .. -28 dB and flat. 9 s loop with a 0.5 s seam inside the 10 s the operator marked.

File name: take 5 s onwards. Operator 2026-09-25, asked which window: '30-42s and 43-55s clipped separately, I'll let you know what dryer is which' — so TWO loops are baked from this recording and the L/R assignment is his, pending. This is the 30-42 s window: -2.4 dBFS flat with ~8 % of samples at full scale (measured per 2 s: 7.8-8.3 % clipped), so the distortion is in the recording and stays in the loop; RMS normalisation lowers it ~17.6 dB. The 5-30 s rise (-14 -> -2.4 dB, motor fundamental fixed at 72-74 Hz) is the microphone approaching, not a spin-up, and is in neither loop.

The 43-55.5 s window of the same recording (see mech_dryer_run_30s): -4.2 .. -4.5 dB, 0.9-1.4 % of samples clipped. Currently the one mech_dryer.tres points at, as an INTERIM default until the operator assigns the two windows to L3C.14 L/R.
'in_operation': running sound only; ramps are generated at runtime. Whole file is -26.5 dB flat after the first 0.5 s.
'in_operation'. Quiet recording (-32 dB flat, peak -13 dB) — normalising lifts it 12 dB. Ramps generated at runtime.
No cutting instruction; 163 s of -28 dB flat. 25 s loop from 5 s in.
No cutting instruction; -17 dB from 1 s to 58 s, then the fade-out at 58-60 s. 25 s loop keeps the irregular crunching from repeating on a short period.
Starter: the pull and the catch, 0-1.25 s; -43 dB gap at 1.0 s, engine from 1.25 s.

Revving: 2.25-5.6 s is 4 dB louder than the idle with the fundamental jumping 256-556 Hz (throttle being worked). Used as the full-throttle loop; it is short, so MachineSound crossfades it over the pitched-up idle rather than playing it alone.
Idle: 5.75-17.25 s at a rock-steady 248 Hz peak and -19 dB — the engine idling.
Shut-off: a last blip at 17.5-19.2 s then the engine dying to -33 dB by 19.75 s.

File name: loop_3x_1m11s-1m14s. Operator 2026-09-25, verbatim: make a new sound from 1:11 to 1:14, 'then it does twice more from 1 minute 11 s to 1 minute 14 s, and then that entire sound of the three, in a sequence, has to loop'. So this is a LOOP, not a one-shot event (an earlier bake made it a 9 s event fired every 90 s — that period was invented and is gone). The window holds one air pulse at 72.65-73.0 s (-16.5 dB peak against a -25 dB bed, 50 ms RMS); the bed at 71.00 s (-24.9 dB) and 73.95 s (-24.4 dB) match, so the wrap is one more 30 ms join like the two inside. 3 x 3.0 s minus three 30 ms joins = 8.91 s, three pulses 2.97 s apart, forever.
Take 1 of 4: onset 0.15 s, crank to 0.55 s, decay to 1.6 s.
Take 4 of 4: onset 5.15 s, runs to the end of the file.
One 0.37 s beep. MachineSound repeats it every alarm_period_s while the wash-line panel holds an unacknowledged fault.
